decisions.reason: A rotation pairing two monogon circles can carry a marked corner to an unmarked interior point. The original corner classes then fail to partition cells and the claimed finite vertex relation is wrong. Requiring the side homeomorphism to preserve marked corners repairs exactly this omission; interval-side maps already preserve endpoints. The closed-relation compact quotient argument and single-cycle links then give the asserted compact second-countable surface and CW cells.

L3 incorrectly calls every region a component of an open set. The published definition permits complements of arbitrary A. Corrected L3 to that definition and made closedness the condition for L5. In the actual proof P and C are compact and closed, and G is a finite union of compact grid edges, so all uses of open-component connectivity are licensed. The finite cycle-space decomposition cancels odd vertices in adjacent groups; their small supporting balls exclude p and q, giving zero crossing parity, in contradiction to a bounded facial walk. First exit along a segment proves the separate boundary-density assertion. Statement unchanged.

The antipodal boundary map preserves, rather than reverses, boundary traversal. Replaced the false step by collars with coordinates (t,r): their seam chart is (t,r) on one side and (t,-r) on the other. The reflection changes the sign relative to the fixed face generator, whereas one ball class itself restricts consistently. A loop using an interior return path and one seam crossing therefore negates its generator and obstructs a global orientation. The antipodal corner pairing, cyclic link, disk-to-hemisphere homeomorphism and cell count 1-1+1 are unchanged and valid.

L5 described only the polygonal subclass rather than the full schema definition. Replaced it by the actual disk/bigon/monogon interface, including corner preservation and conditional affinity. The proof constructs genuine straight-edge polygons by attaching finitely many thin triangles along a dual spanning tree, with affine corner-matching pairings, so its construction already satisfies the stronger subclass. Dual connectivity follows from connected vertex links; the barycentric map has precisely the prescribed fibers, and cyclic links survive contracting tree paths. Also restricted the closed-subset fact to metric spaces; the final homeomorphism uses the already cited compact-to-Hausdorff theorem. Statement unchanged.

The cited closed-subset lemma is metric, so L3 now states its metric hypothesis and L4 uses the already declared general compact-to-Hausdorff theorem directly for quotient sources. The word identities were checked against Gallier–Xu Lemma 6.1 and by following each split/merge. Added explicit radial boundary reparametrization to keep curved or subdivided faces genuine disk representatives; in cancellation rotate the nonempty residue so both X and Z are nonempty, avoiding an illegal circle-to-interval pairing after inverse subdivision. No interface changes or new AC use are needed. The rejected citation error is nonfatal because the general compact-map criterion already supplies its actual quotient use.

The cusp bigon in the rejection admits no polygonal arc starting at its cusp and entering its interior: a straight initial segment has linear rather than quadratic slope there. The old cut was unsupported. The repair first takes the given closed disk to a round disk and carries its corners to antipodal points by a radially extended boundary homeomorphism, conjugating the pairing. A diameter now gives the two actual closed half-disks. Their boundary identifications paste, and the radial extension in step 2.1 matches them to opposite hemispheres. Endpoint classes remain distinct, so the counts are (2,1,1), and opposite-direction seam charts give orientability.

Equal-exponent side pairings use matching boundary parameters, so they preserve boundary direction. Corrected the orientation argument to use inward collars and the seam chart (t,r)/(t,-r); its reflection has opposite signs relative to the common face orientation, forcing negative transport around a loop crossing one seam. Also corrected the b-pair corner list to v2~v3 and v3~v0, which still gives one vertex. The crosscap rewrite of ba^{-1}ba gives bba^{-1}a^{-1}, cyclically relabelled aabb, so the quotient is the defined Klein bottle with Euler characteristic zero.

The identity 2V-E=F+2 is false (a six-cycle gives 6 versus 4), but it is not used in the succeeding derivation. Deleted it. The 2-connected case combines 4F<=2E with V-E+F=2; cut-vertex induction uses f(G)=f(G1)+f(G2)-2 and the one-edge base f=3. Also made the base facial-length count explicit, corrected the accidental assertion that F-prime misses itself, and used clopen component traces to justify drawing connectivity, including isolated vertices. Alexander duality applies to the compact locally contractible finite CW trace; crosscuts yield three theta-complement regions, and finite closed pasting of the Schonflies extensions proves (d). AC qualifications agree with the stated suppliers.

The Statement already quantifies nonempty compact connected boundaryless surfaces, so the open-annulus counterexample does not refute the theorem. The display title nevertheless omitted all those restrictions. Repaired the title to state them explicitly. The forward implication uses homeomorphism invariance; the reverse computes the same genus (2-chi)/2, including zero, or crosscap number 2-chi and applies classification to the same fixed model. The AC hypothesis is explicitly inherited from classification. No Statement/Definition or proof change was needed.
